skills.trigger: When evaluating a focal pulmonary lesion on contrast-enhanced CT to determine if it represents a vascular abnormality such as a pseudoaneurysm.
steps: Assess the attenuation of the lesion relative to adjacent blood vessels (e.g., pulmonary artery branches) to confirm it enhances with contrast, distinguishing it from non-vascular masses like tumors or consolidations.
Evaluate the lesion margins; vascular lesions typically appear well-defined and round/oval, whereas malignancies or infections often have irregular or spiculated borders.
Trace the lesion's connection to the pulmonary vasculature to verify its origin from a pulmonary artery branch.

skills.trigger: When determining the specific lobar location of a pulmonary lesion on a coronal CT image.
steps: Identify the vertical position of the lesion relative to the heart and diaphragm; lesions in the lower zone extending toward the diaphragm are likely in the lower lobes.
Determine laterality by identifying the liver (right) and spleen/stomach (left) to confirm the side of the lesion.

Correlate the lesion's position with the expected anatomical course of the lobar pulmonary arteries to distinguish between middle and lower lobe origins, noting that lower lobe vessels extend more inferiorly and posteriorly.
